_comment: REAL EXCAVATION DATA, unlike the invented fixtures under docs/fixtures/.
Every value below is transcribed from a Poggio Civitate record, and each
carries the record it came from in _sources. Nothing here is estimated,
rounded or filled in: a field with no record is absent rather than guessed.
T111 is the second worked example. T104 (t104-2025-layout.json) shows the
survey-record path succeeding. T111 shows it stopping where the record
stops -- its NE corner has no opening elevation, because that corner was
inside T105's 2024 excavation and there was no undisturbed opening surface

datumNail.label: T111 2025, nail in an oak by the southwest corner (corrected value)

note: Stored there already signed, as 'NW: 204/-32'. The site's cardinal
inversion (South and West negative) was applied before the number
reached the spreadsheet, so it is not applied again here. The same
four corners are written out in the trench book's Trench Layout
section as '204E/32S' and so on, and the two records agree.
Three of the four corners only. The NE corner at 209E/32S has NO
opening elevation in any record and is therefore absent here rather
than filled in.
That is not an oversight. T111 overlaps T105, excavated in 2024, in
its northeastern meters -- '204E/32S ... T111 overlaps with T105
(excavated in 2024) in the NE meters of the trench' -- and Locus 1,
the opening topsoil, 'extends over the entire portion of the trench
that was not previously excavated in 2024'. The northeast quadrant
had no opening surface to measure, so the 1 July elevation list stops
at 205E/32S, the eastern limit of Locus 1.
209E/32S first receives an elevation on 16 July, as Locus 3's NE3 at
27.96 mAE. That is a floor-surface reading taken 15 days and two loci
later, not the trench's opening surface, so it is not used here.
The SW corner's 28.70 mAE is NOT natural relief. It is the crest of a
spoil heap from an earlier season: 'In the southwest corner of the
locus, a dirt dump from previous excavations was excavated along with
Locus 1. The dirt dump sloped significantly in this southwest corner
and was 0.52 m deep.'
'A datum point with an absolute elevation of 29.73 meters on the
master grid has been established on a tree outside of the southwest
corner of the trench.'
CORRECTED on 22 July 2025: 'it was determined that the datum points
established at the beginning of the season were 0.50 m high due to a
transit error. The datum points were reshot and all points from 2025
prior to July 22 were corrected. The datum point for T111 is at an
elevation of 29.23 m A.E.'
29.23 is the value used here, and the Methodology section states the
same figure. Every elevation in this fixture and in t111-2025-loci
and t111-2025-special-finds is on the corrected scale -- see
_known_problems for the evidence that they are.

site_grid.record: T111, 2025, NKD V Trench Book, Trench Layout section
note: 'The trench was triangulated off a longitudinal baseline along grid
line 42 S and along latitudinal grid line 215 E.' T111 is on the
Piano del Tesoro, so the hill grid rather than Vescovado di Murlo.
Named from the corner labels: two corners sharing a cardinal letter
name the wall between them, so NW to NE is the north wall. All four
sides come out 5.00 m, which is what the Trench Layout section says:
'T111 is a 5 meter by 5 meter trench.'

_known_problems: THE EAST WALL CANNOT BE REGISTERED. Its origin corner is NE, which has no
opening elevation, so its surfaceZ is null and the build refuses it. The
other three walls register from surveyed values with no placeholders. This
is the documented refusal working correctly on real data, not a defect in
the fixture.
THE 2024 AND 2025 BASELINES DISAGREE BY 30 cm. From the 30 June entry:
'while triangulating, we noticed a 30cm discrepancy between this year's
baseline and last year's grid; what was projected as 206E in 2024 is 30cm
to the west of what is projected as 206E this year. To avoid a discrepancy
in last year's coordinates of ETAP1, we will use 2024's baseline as our
guide.' So every coordinate here is on the 2024 baseline, deliberately,
and is offset ~0.30 m from a coordinate shot against the 2025 baseline.
Anything combining T111 with a trench that used the 2025 baseline has to
reconcile that offset first.
THE DATUM NAIL'S PLAN POSITION IS RECORDED THREE DIFFERENT WAYS. The
Trench Layout section puts it 'on a tree outside of the southwest corner
of the trench'; the 30 June daily entry puts it on 'a large oak tree with
our datum nail ... in the center of the trench'; the locus descriptions
refer throughout to 'the tree in the southwest'. Its ELEVATION is
consistent across the records at 29.23 mAE corrected. Its easting and
northing are not recorded anywhere, so this fixture states no position
for it beyond the label.
THE 1 JULY CLOSING ELEVATIONS REPEAT THE OPENING ONES AT SW. Both read
28.70 mAE, on a day spent lowering the dirt dump in exactly that corner.
The 2 July closing reads 28.26 mAE there. The 1 July closing figure looks
carried over rather than freshly measured, so only the opening set is
used here.
THE ELEVATIONS ARE ON THE CORRECTED (29.23) SCALE, and the sequence proves
it rather than the record asserting it. The 21 July closing of Locus 3 and
the 22 July opening of Locus 6 -- the day the datum was reshot -- are
continuous: Locus 3 closes at 27.87-28.02 mAE and Locus 6 opens at
27.87-27.99 mAE at points inside it. A 0.50 m step at that boundary would
be unmistakable and there is none. The 22 July note says the corrections
were applied retrospectively to 'all points from 2025 prior to July 22',
and the elevations behave as though they were.
